text: In Descartes' substance dualism, the mind is res cogitans and the body is res extensa. What single essential attribute defines res extensa?
explanation: For Descartes each substance has exactly one essence: res cogitans (mind) is essentially thinking, while res extensa (body) is essentially extended — it occupies space. Thought, free will, and sensation all belong to the thinking substance, not to extended body; that sharp split between the two essences is what generates the interaction problem.
